title: A pasted colour code with a space in front loses its last letter and is refused
what: The colour code box on Branding takes at most 7 characters. When an owner pastes a code copied with a space in front (common when copying from a chat, a design file or a web page), the box keeps the space and cuts off the last letter, so the code becomes five letters long and the box turns red with 'Type a colour code'. The owner sees a correct-looking code being refused.
expected: Spaces around a pasted code are dropped before the length limit applies, so ' #F7D411' becomes '#F7D411' and is accepted.
how_often: when a code is pasted with a space in front
fix_line: Trim the pasted text before keeping it, or allow a few more characters and trim on save

items.reason: Branding reads none of the member fields in field-fill.csv; it reads the gym's own brand fields and name. Crispy Curves (one gym row, gym_id filter): logo filled, saved date filled, name filled, accent and background empty (MettleUp defaults), heading 'normal'.
The Branding screen is the place that asks for logo and colours; every empty field falls back to MettleUp's own look, so nothing waits on it.
No feature here breaks when a brand field is empty: empty accent or background means MettleUp's look by design.

Only text box is the colour code (max 7, autofill off). Codes without #, lower case, 3-letter short codes and a trailing space or semicolon all end as a valid code; a leading space is cut to 5 letters and refused; other-script digits are refused with a clear message. No mobile, name or date boxes in this area; the logo is a file pick.
